claims.text: Data-driven predictive models can enable stable microstructures in RHEA–Cu materials at high temperatures.
A significant positive heat of mixing poses a challenge to combining refractory high-entropy alloys with Cu.
The initial material is a refractory high-entropy alloy containing Cu as a component.
Machine-learning predictive models will optimize alloy composition.
Machine-learning predictive models will optimize processing parameters.
The proposed material is intended for high-temperature environments relevant to nuclear reactors.
Machine-learning models can identify compositions that mitigate the effects of positive heat of mixing.
Machine-learning models can identify processing conditions that mitigate the effects of positive heat of mixing.
Mitigating the effects of positive heat of mixing will improve microstructural stability.
Model-guided composition and processing will improve the microstructural stability of RHEA–Cu materials.
Improved microstructural stability will facilitate use of RHEA–Cu materials in nuclear-reactor cooling systems.
Current formation of RHEA–Cu composite structures is hindered by significant positive heat of mixing.
The proposed hypothesis applies specifically to RHEA–Cu systems at high temperature.
Experimental validation is required to determine whether the predictive models overcome the heat-of-mixing challenge.
